transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… student health told me I had to come. They said my weight is too low to clear me for the youth workshops, and that it’s been dropping. I don’t know… I feel like I’ve just been busy and focused, so it didn’t seem like a big thing to me.
Can you tell me about your eating habits lately? Have you been intentionally losing weight or changing your diet in any specific way?

I mean… I guess I’ve been more careful. I usually just have coffee before studio, and then maybe a few bites of something from the café if people are around. I don’t really like eating bread or oily stuff. It feels like it would kind of… undo the control I’ve been trying to keep.
Have you been avoiding any other specific foods or food groups, or do you feel anxious about eating certain things?

Yeah… I guess bread, oily things. Anything that feels heavy. I sort of plan my day so I don’t really have to eat much—coffee before studio, maybe just a few bites if people are around. It makes me anxious, like if I eat those things I’m losing the control I’ve been trying to keep.
Have you been deliberately avoiding eating certain foods or restricting your intake to prevent gaining weight, even if you feel underweight or people tell you you’re too thin?

Yeah… I mean, I guess I do. I kind of plan my whole day around not really eating much—coffee before studio, maybe a few bites from the café if people are watching. And I avoid bread or anything oily… it feels like it would undo the control I’ve worked for.

latest_inference.note: The patient's responses confirm intentional restriction of food intake, avoidance of specific food groups, and anxiety around eating, particularly to maintain control and avoid weight gain. These are key features of Anorexia Nervosa (F50.0). Other candidates (E40, E41) are ruled out as the clinical picture is not consistent with malnutrition due to deficiency or other specified nutritional deficiencies).
